title: Mihakk session
description: A fuzzing session: its authorised scope, its limits, and its completeness. Shared contract between the Go engine and the Python orchestrator.

status.description: completed = ran to the end with every event accounted for. incomplete = finished but events were lost, so results are a subset. interrupted = the engine or the stream died before the session ended. stopped = an operator used the kill switch.

host.description: Exact hostname or IP. Wildcards are refused: they make it too easy to authorise something you do not own.

allowed_addresses.description: Specific restricted addresses this target may resolve to: single IPs or narrow CIDRs (IPv4 /24 or narrower, IPv6 /120 or narrower). Broad ranges such as 10.0.0.0/8 are refused, Link-local (including the cloud metadata address 169.254.169.254), multicast, unspecified and broadcast addresses can never be authorised by any entry: the engine refuses such a config outright, and refuses the address again at dial time. Public addresses need no entry. This list is part of the scope digest, so editing it invalidates the authorisation acknowledgement.

limits.description: Every ceiling is mandatory and must be positive. There is deliberately no 'unlimited' value.

max_session_duration.description: Go duration string ("10m") or bare seconds.

authorization.description: No session starts without this. The acknowledgement is bound to one exact scope digest, so it cannot be replayed against a wider scope.

statement.const: I am authorised to test the targets listed in this scope.
statement.description: Exact text, not a boolean, so the acknowledgement appears verbatim in the audit log.

completeness.description: Whether the orchestrator saw every event the engine produced. When complete is false, the session and every report derived from it MUST be labelled as partial: the result set is a subset of what the engine observed, and absence of a finding proves nothing.

events_dropped.description: Events the engine produced that never reached the orchestrator, counted by sequence gaps and by the engine's own ring-buffer overflow counter.
